**Observations on the test image:**
- Single young mango leaf, mostly green, elongated
- Leaf margins show irregular, bumpy/notched projections along the edges
- Some brownish discoloration at tips of marginal protrusions
- Leaf is slightly curled

**Analysis:**
- **Cutting_Weevil** reference shows extreme stripping — leaves almost completely removed, leaving only petioles/midribs. The test image still has full leaf tissue, so this doesn't match.
- **Gall_Midge** reference shows round blister-shaped galls protruding along leaf margins and surface, creating an irregular bumpy margin — this matches closely with the test image's irregular, raised projections along the margin edges.
- **Sooty_Mould** shows dark black surface coating — not present here.
- No white powder (Powdery_Mildew), no dark sunken lesions (Anthracnose), no raised black angular spots (Bacterial_Canker), no bark discoloration/gum (Die_Back).

The bumpy, blister-like protrusions along the leaf margins with slight discoloration is characteristic of **Gall_Midge** gall formations.
